items.description: Manage the PostgreSQL databases your Connector can reach — add them, switch between them, and see which one is currently active
items.content:
Your Connections

Each database your Connector can reach appears as a connection. You switch between them from the selector at the top of the Data Explorer.

---

Picking a database

The selector groups your connections and marks which ones are online. Schema Weaver selects an available one for you when you arrive, and remembers your last choice for next time.

Only online connections are selectable — if the Connector is stopped, its databases won't appear as available.

items.title: The Connector
items.description: The Schema Weaver Connector is a small service that runs inside your environment and reaches your PostgreSQL database on your behalf — so your credentials never have to leave it

headings.title: Why it runs on your side

items.content:
The Connector

Schema Weaver reaches your database through the Connector — a small service you run yourself, on the machine that already has access to PostgreSQL.

items.title: Security Architecture
items.description: Schema Weaver's connector security architecture — Local Credential Boundary (LCB), Connector-Enforced Read-Only Execution (CERO), and Zero-Ingress Network Isolation

headings.title: The Connector as the Execution Security Boundary
3. Separation of Credential Ownership & Execution Authority
5. Controlled Data Plane & Transient Query Results

items.content:
Security Architecture

Schema Weaver's database connector is built around two core architectural principles:

- Local Credential Boundary (LCB): Customer database credentials remain completely isolated inside the customer's private environment.
- Connector-Enforced Read-Only Execution (CERO): Read-only database access is independently enforced at the connector boundary, never entrusted solely to the cloud or an AI model.

Together, LCB and CERO establish a clear separation between credential own

items.title: Sharing with Your Team
items.description: Give teammates access to a Connector and the databases behind it, without sharing credentials, and control who can manage it

headings.title: Managing shared Connectors in Team Settings

items.content:
Sharing with Your Team

A Connector can be shared with your team so colleagues can query the same databases you have. They never see your credentials — they get access to the Connector, which already has them.

---

What a teammate gets

Access to every database that Connector reaches, through the Data Explorer:

- Browse tables and inspect column statistics
- Run read-only queries
- Ask Resona AI questions against your data
- Build dashboards

They cannot read or write your database credentials

items.title: Workspace Editing
items.description: Resona AI makes targeted, surgical edits to your SQL project files — single-block patches, multi-change file edits, and cross-file refactoring with full preview and rollback
items.content:
Workspace Editing

When Resona AI edits your SQL files it does not regenerate entire files from scratch. It finds the exact block that needs to change and replaces only that — leaving everything else untouched. It can make multiple changes to a single file in one go, or apply edits across several files at once, with full rollback if anything goes wrong.

items.title: Resona AI in the ER Diagram
items.description: Analyze tables, schema groups, and your entire schema with Resona AI directly from the ER Diagram — generate SQL, suggest indexes, check normalization, and apply changes instantly
items.content:
Resona AI in the ER Diagram

Resona AI is embedded directly into the ER Diagram at three levels: individual tables, schema groups, and the full schema. Each level opens a chat panel anchored by a dashed blue edge to its subject — you can ask questions, request SQL, and apply generated changes without leaving the diagram.

> Quick links: [Open SQL Editor](https://sql-editor.schemaweaver.dev/) · [ER Diagram Overview](/sql-editor/er-diagram) · [Resona AI Assistant](/sql-editor/ai-assistant)

items.title: Grouping & Schema Clusters
items.description: Cluster your ER diagram nodes by PostgreSQL schema namespace — resizable group containers, schema color coding, per-group stats, and lock mode
items.content:
Grouping & Schema Clusters

When Cluster by Schema is enabled, the ER Diagram groups all nodes by their PostgreSQL schema namespace into visually distinct containers. Tables, views, functions, and other objects that belong to `auth`, `billing`, `public`, `inventory` — or any other schema in your project — are enclosed in their own labeled group. This makes it immediately clear which domain each object belongs to and eliminates the visual noise of a flat diagram with hundreds of nodes.

> Qui

items.title: Path Analysis
items.description: Instantly find the shortest JOIN path between PostgreSQL tables using BFS and Dijkstra algorithms. Visualize relationship chains in the SW ER Diagram.
items.content:
Path Analysis

Path Analysis finds the shortest foreign-key relationship chain between any two tables in your schema. Instead of manually tracing JOIN paths through a dense diagram, you select a start table and an end table — the diagram highlights every intermediate table and edge you would need to traverse to connect them.

> Quick links: [Open SQL Editor](https://sql-editor.schemaweaver.dev/) · [ER Diagram Overview](/sql-editor/er-diagram)

![Path Analysis active in the ER Diagram showi

items.title: Visibility & Node Types
items.description: Control exactly which PostgreSQL object types and which schema namespaces are shown in the ER Diagram — declutter large schemas and focus on what matters
items.content:
Visibility & Node Types

The ER Diagram supports every PostgreSQL object type — tables, views, materialized views, functions, enums, domains, roles, sequences, extensions, and RLS policies. On a real production schema this can mean dozens or hundreds of extra nodes beyond your core tables. The Visibility controls let you show only what you need, making large diagrams readable and layout faster.

> Quick links: [Open SQL Editor](https://sql-editor.schemaweaver.dev/) · [ER Diagram Overview](/s

items.title: ER Diagram
items.description: Visualize your entire PostgreSQL schema as a live, interactive entity-relationship diagram — all object types supported, updates in real time as you write SQL
items.content:
ER Diagram

The ER Diagram is a live, interactive visualization of your entire PostgreSQL schema. Every object — tables, views, materialized views, functions, enums, domains, sequences, roles, extensions, and RLS policies — renders as a node on a pannable, zoomable canvas. Foreign-key relationships appear as directed edges. The diagram updates in real time as you type SQL with no manual refresh required, and scales to schemas with thousands of tables.

> Quick links: [Open SQL Editor](https:
